The must-sees

5 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Palace · 1760

    Amalienborg

    Built in the 1750s for noble families, Amalienborg became the royal home after Christiansborg burned in 1794. The Royal Life Guard is changed here every day.

    Look for

    In the middle of the square, Frederik V rides a bronze horse, the king who founded this district.

  2. 02
    Civic building · 1928

    Christiansborg

    This is the third Christiansborg on the islet of Slotsholmen. Ruins of the earlier castles survive in the cellars beneath it.

    Look for

    In front of the palace, an equestrian statue shows Frederik VII, the king who gave Denmark its constitution in 1849.

  3. 03
    Waterfront · 1673

    Nyhavn

    Nyhavn was dug in the 1670s as a merchant harbor. Sailors’ bars once lined the quay; today the painted houses are the city’s front porch.

    Look for

    Find the plaques at numbers 18, 20 and 67. Hans Christian Andersen lived in all three houses.

  4. 04
    Palace · 1633

    Rosenborg Castle

    Rosenborg began as a summer house in 1606 and grew into a Dutch Renaissance castle. The treasury in the basement holds the Danish crown jewels.

    Look for

    In the Long Hall, the coronation throne is made of narwhal tusk and guarded by three life-size silver lions.

  5. 05
    Venue · 1843

    Tivoli Gardens

    Georg Carstensen is said to have told the king that when people are amused they do not think of politics. Tivoli opened in 1843 and still mixes rides, pantomime and gardens.

    Look for

    Find the old wooden roller coaster from 1914. A brakeman still rides on each train to slow it down on the drops.
